text:
Kyle Connor has 17 goals in 22 games, fifth in the league in wins added by goals, and he passed 700 career points this month. When Winnipeg erased a four-goal deficit in Chicago, he and Mark Scheifele were the two who scored in the shootout.

The shooting is the asterisk. He's at 18% on 12.9 expected goals, up from 14% last season. The chances are genuine, he's one of the league's busiest shooters with 96 shots, but that finishing rate rarely lasts. Our range for his season sits between 41 and 59 goals, so even a cooler second half lands him somewhere very good.

How he gets there hasn't changed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 66% of his entries last season and getting 6.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 87th percentile. He doesn't need many touches to matter. The thing to watch is his assist total (9), which is light for a top-line winger and the likeliest place for his production to grow once the goals slow.
headline: Connor's goals are real, the rate isn't
